directive.quote: Same language, so it's a SOURCE_FIRST_PORT: byte copy first, then edits.

old_copy.deleted_with: the cloud job that deletes the old sign-in files, with src/mail-admission.mjs and src/mail-settings.json

preserve: the sender comes only from the mail row (the one from, or a written email's owner row of senders.rows); a caller adds only its reply_to
every email to one address is written down under it, a sign-in or share code without its subject
a send over a per-person limit for its kind is not sent and answers limited with the limit's words
a proof account's own address is never handed to the provider, is still written down, and spends none of the day
the allowance is taken before the provider is asked; once only keep_back of the day's most remain only the kept_for kinds go, and the day's most stops every kind
only a code the provider's row lists as refused before dispatch gives the allowance back; any other failure answers unknown, keeps counting and is never sent again blindly
a provider saying its own day is full fills the day
a written email goes as a BCC to the account's own address, never twice to the same person, and answers its sent copy
subscription mail carries its one-click unsubscribe headers and its visible consent footer, and refuses before delivery without them
allowed_deltas: the rules are the account's own mail-settings record settings:mail, copied from read-data/mail-settings.json the first time, not one file for every account; it ships with no sender and no postal address

the sent log and the day are the account's own mail-sent and mail-day records through the records door, one write conditioned on what was read in place of the shared pool's SQL transaction (the older owner's src/mail-admission.mjs: its policy is kept here, its tables are not)

the provider is a row of read-data/message-providers.json reached through the sending seam, and how its refusals read is the mail row's providers entry, not a Cloudflare Email Sending binding and its codes
the older owner's KV path before the shared pool, the proof inbox keeper and the receiving side's refusal of an address are not moved: nothing here keeps KV or receives mail
the email is drawn by the sending seam in the person's look, not by this file
banned_substitutions: a sender taken from the request
sending again a message whose first send may have gone
a code's subject in a record
a limit counted after the provider was asked
